z.note: The standard-normal cumulative distribution gives the area to the left of the entered value.

t.note: The subscript alpha denotes the upper-tail probability; nu is the degrees of freedom.

chi_square.note: Critical values use upper-tail probability alpha and degrees of freedom nu.

f.note: The numerator degrees of freedom come first; the denominator degrees of freedom come second.

binomial_pmf.note: Independent trials with constant success probability; the count ranges from zero through n.

binomial_cmf.note: The cumulative probability includes the entered count.

poisson_pmf.note: Lambda is the expected count in the observation interval.

poisson_cmf.note: The cumulative probability includes the entered count.

exponential.note: Standardized time is rate times elapsed time; mu is mean lifetime. F is failure probability and S is survival probability.

studentized_range.note: Tukey critical values use the number of groups and error degrees of freedom.

duncan.note: Duncan uses the number of ordered means spanned and a range-dependent significance level.

control_chart.note: Factors depend on subgroup size. The displayed mean limits apply to an X-bar/R chart.

sigma_level.note: The shifted convention includes both tails. Centered PPM is rounded to a whole number; shifted PPM to one decimal.

median_ranks.note: Bernard’s approximation for complete, ordered failure data; this does not handle censoring.

normal_scores.note: Blom’s plotting-position approximation transformed by the standard-normal inverse CDF.

tolerance_one.note: The inverse is the noncentral t quantile at confidence gamma, with degrees of freedom nu and noncentrality delta. P is minimum population coverage. Each bound is one-sided; combining them does not give the corresponding two-sided tolerance interval.

tolerance_two.note: Howe’s approximation. The chi-square subscript denotes a LOWER-tail quantile here, unlike the upper-tail column headings in the chi-square reference table. P is minimum population coverage and gamma is confidence.
